prerequisites: Mathematics from secondary education with at least 6 hours of mathematics lessons.

learning_outcomes.text: Acquire insight into (finite) algebraic structures and be able to recognize them and use their properties as they occur in engineering applications in the field of information and communication technology (data structures, cryptography, coding theory, mathematical models, ...).
Be able to work smoothly with these structures and their properties rather than focusing on the theoretical study and rigorously proving all properties.
Learn to use these concepts and methodologies in exercises and assignments.

syllabus_topics: relations (including equivalence relations and order relations)
functions (injection, surjection, bijection, composition of functions), mappings
propositional logic, truth tables, normal forms
isomorphism (relation between sets, logic, and Boolean algebra)
definition, Abelian group, cyclic group, permutation group
order of an element, exponent of the group
subgroups (normal divisor), quotient structure, Lagrange's theorem
definition, ring with unity, zero divisors, cancellation law, modular arithmetic
Euclidean domains, Euclidean algorithm, Bezout-Bachet theorem
ideals, quotient structure, prime ideal, maximal ideal, principal ideal
definition, finite fields, characteristic of a field
polynomial ideal, quotient structure, extension fields
error correcting code of the CD player

assessment_methods.method: True/false statements with proofs or counterexamples and corrections

assessment_rules: The exam consists of three questions. The first two questions are exercises, each counting for 5 points out of 20 (25% of the total). A third question for 10 points (50% of the total) involves 7 statements for which it must be indicated whether they are true or false; if true, they must be proven; if false, a counterexample must be given and the statement must be corrected. The exam is open book; Part I of the course text may be used, but no solved exercises may be added. Part II of the course text with solved exercises may not be used.
bibliography: Part II of the course text contains solved exercises.
